expectations.evidence: First sentence is a calibrated nontechnical verdict: 'it's not as bad as "23 vulnerabilities" sounds, but there are two real ones we should fix fast, and one process gap worth closing.' Scanner headline deferred to next paragraph.
Mentions '23 issues (2 critical, 5 high, 11 moderate, 5 low)' but immediately defuses: 'most of it is noise — 17 of the 23 are in dev/build tooling...'; actionable subset (3 things) separated.
SSRF explained as 'someone could hand us a malicious URL'; auth layer as 'verifies session tokens on every login'; no unexplained security jargon.
Order: 1) jsonwebtoken (today), 2) axios (this week), 3) lodash hygiene, then others/maintenance — exactly fixture recommendation.
Counts: 2 critical, 5 high, 11 moderate, 5 low, 23 total. Estimates: 1-2h (jsonwebtoken), 2-3h (axios), 5 min (lodash). All present and match fixture.

jsonwebtoken: 'exploiting it would require conditions we don't currently expose' (fixture); axios: 'fetches a user-submitted URL for avatar imports'; lodash: 'only used in a script that generates our sitemap, not in anything a user request touches'. No invented paths or confidence upgrades.
17 of 23 noise + 3 real + 4 dev-only high (implied in 'other 4 of the 5 high ones') reconciles with 23 total; '11 moderate and 5 low' accounted for in non-urgent bucket.
Process gap (no Dependabot/Renovate) is mentioned but no time/effort estimate is given for setting it up; remains unstated/explicitly unknown.
Short opening, then 3 numbered bullets, brief exploitation check, one gap line, one-line net close. No advisory dump, no formulaic section headers, no trailing recap.
